Personal style is a practice.

Less about following a look. More about noticing what feels like you.

Nov 20262 min read

Chapters

  1. Look beyond the reference image.
  2. Document what changes.
  3. Make space for experimentation.

Personal style is not a fixed destination. It shifts with the places you go, the people you meet, and the ideas you are working through. That is what makes it personal.

Look beyond the reference image.

When something catches your eye, name the detail that does the work. The shape of a sleeve, an unlikely colour pairing, the tension between a polished surface and something worn. Being specific helps you turn inspiration into a decision rather than a copy.

Try combining references from different places. A film still, a building, a favourite album cover. Style becomes more interesting when it is a conversation between influences.

Document what changes.

Take a photograph of an everyday look, not only the special occasion. Over time, patterns will appear. You may keep returning to the same silhouette or colour, or discover that the unexpected choice felt the most natural.

The details you choose are a way of telling your own story.

Make space for experimentation.

Change one thing. Borrow a shape, try a different proportion, or put together pieces you would usually keep apart. Small experiments take the pressure off getting a whole identity right.

Share what you learned, not only what you wore. A conversation about process makes room for other people to find their own way in.
